body.text: Melbourne Cup 2026 live: Hopewell Rock favourite, Asterix scratched at Flemington
British horse Hopewell Rock begins Melbourne Cup Day as the favourite for the race that stops the nation.
Chris Waller-trained Asterix has been scratched from the Cup after stewards deemed medication had been used on the horse today. Waller explained it was a simple mistake in the heat of the moment.
The four-year-old colt is one of 24 horses preparing to start the 166th edition of the Cup at Flemington this afternoon.
Follow all the action of Melbourne Cup Day at Flemington on the live blog below.

How does the track rating system work?
If you're new to racing, or if you only tune in once a year on a day like today, the description of the track rating may confuse you.
The system uses a scale of 10 different ratings, from 1 to 10.
Rating 1 and 2 are Firm, with 1 a dry hard track and 2 a firm track. Ratings 3 and 4 are Good, with 3 a better covering of grass and 4 a track with some give in it.
For everyday races, normally track managers aim to have the track at a Good 3 or 4.
Then ratings 5 to 7 are Soft, meaning that there is more moisture and give in the track. By the time you get to a 7, it's a more rain-affected track that will start to chop up with the horses racing.
Right now we are at a Soft 5, which means there is some moisture in the track but it's not deteriorating yet. in fact the lack of recent rain means we could see an upgrade to a Good 4 at some stage.
The last three ratings — 8 to 10 — are Heavy.
At this point, you need to have had a lot of rain, and increasing levels of deterioration in the track.
When it gets to a Heavy track, only so-called "mudlarks" will cope with it. Organisers will be hoping we don't get to that stage today.
Former Wallaby Nathan Charles wants to do things 'for the first time'
Former Wallaby Nathan Charles, the only person with cystic fibrosis to play a contact sport professionally, is at Flemington.
He was diagnosed this year with motor neurone disease (MND), and is now using his platform to help others.
He has just been interviewed by the Nine Network about his diagnosis and his future.

"In life, everyone has adversity. I've always been a believer in you should be judged not by how you fall over, but instead how you stand back up. And it's a really unfortunate circumstance," he said.
"But it is my journey and I've just got to keep on moving forward.
"Firstly, it was the question of 'Why me?' And then my second question was, 'How long have I got?'
"I sort of took the week to get my emotions together.
"And then I just thought, you know what, I gotta flip the script.
"Instead of doing things for the last time I want to start doing things for the first time.
"And I want to provide inspiration and hope to young Australians that they can achieve in the face of adversity."
You are a champion, Nathan.
Peyton wins fourth race at Flemington by a neck
Rider Zac Lloyd has ridden Peyton to a terrific win in the fourth at Flemington.
Over the 1,000m down the Flemington straight, Peyton chased down longtime leader Fovea to snatch the win with a final stride.
That is a win for jockey Lloyd, who is riding the Melbourne Cup favourite Hopewell Rock.
"We needed every bit of that Flemington straight. Credit to my bloke, he dug in and chased [Fovea]."
Chris Waller says 'very simple mistake' led to Melbourne Cup scratching
The biggest news so far today is the scratching of Chris Waller-trained Asterix.
The horse was found to have Penetrene, a medication for sprains and muscle relief — applied to its forelegs.
Because that is a medication, it is illegal to apply without permission on race day.
Waller has told News Corp journalist Gilbert Gardiner that it was an honest mistake from the person who looks after Asterix.

"The horse gets the same treatment every day, it's a very basic liniment most stables use and I guess the pressure of race day, the person that looks after the horse, put it on his legs right in front of the security guard, nothing to hide," Waller said.
"The pressure of raceday, a very simple mistake.
"Nothing was hidden, the security guard was right there, as soon as it happened we knew there was a problem.

"It's not her fault. I've got to wear the responsibility. It's my team. It's rare for us to make mistakes but the pressure of raceday, you can't explain how it affects everybody. Everyone is on edge on Melbourne Cup Day and you think a little bit differently."

Stewards inquiry as Melbourne Cup contender scratched
— reporting by AAP

High-profile trainer Chris Waller has been questioned by stewards after his Melbourne Cup contender Asterix was found to have had the medication Penetrene administered to both forelegs in its stable just hours before Australia's greatest race.
Asterix, part-owned by former New Zealand international cricketer Mark Greatbatch, was scratched from today's $10 million Flemington showpiece.
Penetrene is generally allowed to be used on horses, except on race days.
"Penetrene is a topical product marketed as an anti-inflammatory and analgesic liniment," Racing Victoria said in a statement.
"Penetrene is used topically on horses for symptomatic relief of muscle strains, sprains and muscle soreness.
"Any substance administered to a horse on raceday, including any topical application amongst any other route of administration is considered a medication."
Stewards will continue their inquiries into the circumstances with Waller later on Tuesday.
Asterix's scratching leaves Waller with only one contender - $21 fancy Soul Of Spain - in the Cup. Asterix had been a $51 chance.
It also leaves 2020 Cup-winning jockey Jye McNeil without a ride in Flemington's $10 million showpiece.
McNeil rebounded from the news to finish second with Royal Press in the opening race on the card, behind Damian Lane on Amelia's Affair.
Meanwhile, popular jockey Harry Coffey has arrived at Flemington to ride Shockletz in the Cup, just two days after having a plate inserted to repair his fractured collarbone.
Coffey required surgery after his scary Victoria Derby day fall, but was all smiles as he flapped his 'wing' at punters when he walked towards the mounting yard.
Rival jockeys lauded Coffey's bravery after he was declared fit by Racing Victoria's chief medical officer Dr Ben Barresi.
"They always say jockeys are made of different stuff and he's proving that," said Rachel King, who will partner So You Are in the Cup.
"It just proves how much it means to us jockeys ... Melbourne Cup day is the biggest day of the year."
Superstar jockey James McDonald, who will ride Trustyourinstinct for Irish trainer O'Brien and billionaire owner-breeder JP McManus, rates Shockletz among the main challengers.
"(Coffey) is tougher than most of us," McDonald said.
"It's like a grand final for us jockeys and trainers. This is the race that stops the nation, so we'd get up for anything."
Robbie Williams and colourful frocks brighten Melbourne Cup under grey skies
Some early rain is predicted to give way to a mild spring day for the 166th running of the Melbourne Cup at Flemington for the race that stops a nation.

Billycart wins the third race at Flemington
Billycart has taken the win in the 3-year-old race over 1,800.
A lovely ride from Dean Yendall, who needed to slice through the field and ran over the top of Mister Whiskers to win.
Why was Asterix scratched?
What was asterix scratched? - Mark
What was asterix scratched?

G'day Mark.
Stewards found that a product called Penetrene was used on the horse this morning.
It is a topical product to relieve muscle strains, sprains and muscle soreness.
However, anything considered a medication, which Penetrene is, is not allowed on race day unless authorised by the stewards.
30 years since Saintly's Melbourne Cup win for Bart Cummings
While we're all about today's big race, sometimes it's good to look back at some of the great stories that have come out of the Melbourne Cup.
Thirty years ago this week, the "horse from heaven", Saintly, ridden by Darren Beadman, won at Flemington to give "Cups king" Bart Cummings his 10th victory.
Cummings, the unchallenged master of training Cup winners, always had a plan. But he broke his own hard-and-fast rules to guide Saintly's campaign.
Cummings's long-time track rider, Joe Agresta, spoke to the ABC about those days and his initial thoughts about the horse.
"He was a nice horse, but he was a gangly type of three-year-old," Agresta says.
When he turned four, things changed and the big-striding chestnut gelding won the Australian Cup earlier in the year before an unlikely win in the Cox Plate leading into the big day at Flemington.

Yauson wins race two on Cup Day — the Community Handicap
The second race has been run and won, and it's a victory for the training partnership of Gai Waterhouse and Adrian Bott.
For the Community Handicap over 2,000m, Yauson was drawn out wide in barrier 21. With Jordan Childs on board, Yauson was pushed forward early to sit about second.
The horse stayed close to the lead for most of the race before pushing clear down the straight for an impressive win over Mr O'Reilly, with Military Academy third.
Yausun was two or three off the fence — it was interesting that not too many managed to make up ground from the back of the field in the long Flemington straight.
Waterhouse was thrilled with the win and she teased the fact that apparently she will be on stage with Robbie Williams later today!

Asterix (9), trained by Chris Waller, has been scratched from the big race.
Key Event
Amelia's Affair wins first race of the day — Maribyrnong Plate
The first race of Melbourne Cup Day has been run, and it has been won by Amelia's Affair.
Ridden by Damien Lane, Amelia's Affair took the lead early in the 1,000m sprint down the Flemington straight, and was never challenged.
A lovely ride from barrier 1, and it was interesting to see that all horses went to the grandstand-side rail.
"She relaxed beautifully and never really looked lost … I think she's going to take us on a good ride," trainer Annabel Archibald said.

What are the conditions at Flemington today?
There has been some rain around Melbourne in the past 24 hours, which has resulted in the Flemington track starting Cup Day rated as a Soft 5.
The weather is expected to improve as the day goes on, with a top of about 18 degrees Celsius.
Currently, the temp is about 15C.
The rail is in 3 metres for Cup Day.

There is no set time for when a horse needs to be scratched or not.
Essentially, as soon as a horse is deemed unfit to run, that horse is scratched immediately. Then that news filters through quite quickly as well.
So, when it happens, we will let you know straight away on the live blog.
